subject: 🏃 Monday — Hip Complex Circuit (Wk 3)
html:
Tomorrow: 20-min Hip Complex Circuit — post-B2B mobility flush. No running, no load. This is active recovery after a strong 15K on hilly terrain. Exercises: 90/90 switches, adductor rockbacks, foam rolling quads/IT band, plus the PT mobility flush (foam roller T-spine extensions, standing lunges with hip IR + extension).

Knee was 2/5 at Bay to Breakers — double the mobility flush tonight and tomorrow. Per protocol: foam roll quads/IT band 2 min each side (not the usual 1 min), glute bridges 2×15, banded clamshells 2×15, 90/90 PAILs 45 sec each side. The knee didn't progress during or after the race, which is the key signal — but 2/5 means extra tissue work, not dismissal.

Focus cue: Spend time on the foam roller. You just ran 9.3 miles with 533 ft of gain including a surprise Point Lobos climb at mile 8 — your quads and hip flexors absorbed real eccentric load on those descents through Golden Gate Park. The mobility work tomorrow isn't optional filler; it's what keeps Tuesday's easy 4-miler feeling smooth instead of wooden.

Context: Week 3 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation — 10 weeks to SF Marathon. This week is a normal build week (not a deload). Tuesday is an easy 4 mi at 9:15–9:30 as post-B2B recovery — no track intervals this week. Full-Rx strength returns Wednesday. The May 30 PAL 10K is 13 days out and will be the real fitness calibration with the Polar H10 on a flat course.

Tonight: Hydrate well — you raced and probably ran a sodium deficit despite the LMNT. Get to bed early. The 48 g/hr fueling data and knee-2/5 reading are logged. Good race today — the fast-finish capacity is real, and we'll quantify it properly at the PAL 10K.
